subject: Renewal amendment: phasing 8→16 GPUs with split billing & throughput SLA
messages:
From: Elaine Brooks <elaine@skycloud.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: SkyCloud Procurement <procurement@skycloud.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — ask about going to 16 GPUs in renewal

Hi Sofia,

Hope you’re well — our contract renewal is coming up in late June. We’ve been really happy with the performance on the current reserved pool (8 GPUs) but our Q4 roadmap includes heavier batch inference for a new feature and we expect a steady 2x increase in token throughput.

Before we commit, a couple of questions:
- Can we phase the capacity to 16 GPUs at renewal but have the billing split across months (so we only pay full 16-GPU commit after activation)?
- What throughput guarantees can Redwood provide if we pin 16 GPUs as the reserved pool? We need predictable p50/p95 latency for customer-facing endpoints.
- Any ops runbook for staged activation (we prefer a 2-week ramp with 4-hour rollback windows).

If you can send an amendment draft and an ops playbook, I’ll loop in finance/ops on our side.

Thanks,
Elaine
Director of Platform Engineering
SkyCloud AI
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Brooks <elaine@skycloud.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — ask about going to 16 GPUs in renewal

Hi Elaine — great to hear from you and congrats on the roadmap. Short answers first: yes, we can structure a phased activation with split billing, and we can commit to a throughput guardrail tied to the reserved 16-GPU pool with clear p50/p95 targets and an operational rollback plan.

I’m attaching an amendment draft and an ops activation checklist for review. High level proposal:
- Contract amendment: monthly commit increases from 8→12 for months 1–2, then 16 from month 3 onward (option to accelerate). Billing will be pro-rated for the partial months.
- Throughput SLA: target p50 latency for your primary inference route <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms under the committed throughput profile (we’ll include signal-based fallback to a lower-cost region if sustained overcommit).
- Ops: 2-week ramp, daily health checks, KV cache warm-up plan, and 4-hour rollback windows.

If you’re comfortable, I can route the amendment to procurement and have Ben join for commercial details.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: SkyCloud Procurement <procurement@skycloud.ai>, Elaine Brooks <elaine@skycloud.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Pricing & commit structure for 8→16 GPU renewal (SKC-2028-REN-0421)

Elaine / Procurement team — following Sofia’s note, wanted to outline the commercial side so procurement has clarity.

Proposal summary:
- Term: 12 months starting on the renewal effective date.
- Commit schedule: Months 1–2 = 12 GPUs (pro-rated), Month 3+ = 16 GPUs (full monthly commit).
- Billing model: Split billing option allows SkyCloud to pay 60% of the delta (the incremental cost from 8→16) in months 1–2, then 100% in month 3 onward. This reduces cash shock while aligning activation.
- One-time activation fee: $5,000 to cover staged activation runbook and extra engineering support during ramp (waivable for annual prepay).
- Credits: We can offer a 10% commit credit if SkyCloud signs a 24-month extension instead of 12 months.

We’ll capture the exact numbers in the amendment PDF attached. Dev is copied for technical ops scope.

Questions for procurement: any required PO/formal PO number and a preferred signatory?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elaine Brooks <elaine@skycloud.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Ops activation plan & rollback details

Hi all — attaching the ops-activation-plan.xlsx (summary below). I’ll own the runbook during ramp. Key points:

- Warm-up: run KV cache prefill across representative routes 24–48 hours before first capacity bump.
- Ramp windows: three increments — +2 GPUs day 0, +4 GPUs day 3, +2 GPUs day 7 (to reach 16). Each increment followed by 12–24 hour validation at target load.
- Monitoring & alarms: end-to-end latency SLO checks, token-rate monitors, GPU utilization, and tail-latency alerts.
- Rollback: immediate deactivation option within 4 hours of detected SLA degradation; automatic traffic split back to 8-GPU pool if sustained.

Elaine, if that schedule looks good we’ll plan the first bump for the renewal week and provide a shared dashboard access for your ops team.

—Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: SkyCloud Procurement <procurement@skycloud.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Brooks <elaine@skycloud.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Jun 2028 14:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & commit structure for 8→16 GPU renewal (SKC-2028-REN-0421)

Ben — thanks, we appreciate the phased invoice approach. A few items from finance:
- Please include a sample invoice showing month-by-month pro-rated charges so we can route to accounting.
- Confirm whether the activation fee is invoiced on month 1 or after final activation.
- We will need Redwoods’ standard SOC2 attestation and service addendum (AUP) included as attachments to the amendment.

Assuming those items are provided we can put this on the next procurement board for approval. PO number will be provided once board approves.

Regards,
SkyCloud Procurement
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Brooks <elaine@redwood.ai>, SkyCloud Procurement <procurement@skycloud.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal amendment: phasing 8→16 GPUs with split billing & throughput SLA

Thanks — great progress. I’ve attached the updated amendment (redwood-amendment-draft-v3.pdf) with: the pro-forma invoice, payment timing (activation fee invoiced upon signing), and links to SOC2 + AUP. We also added a one-time 2-week credit for any SLA misses during the ramp window.

If procurement is satisfied we can issue the DocuSign link today and schedule the first activation bump for the week of June 20. Elaine — want to confirm that date works for your release calendar.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
